candidates.title: Rare thunderstorm with lightning strikes wows southern B.C., causing havoc at Vancouver airport
candidates.description: Lightning strikes lit up the skies across B.C.'s South Coast overnight in a rare display as a severe thunderstorm passed over the region, snarling traffic at Vancouver International Airport and causing flight issues in the process.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: 'Effectively, we're out of business': U.S. tariffs cut Manitoba honey farm off from vast majority of customers
candidates.description: Osee Podolsky, general manager at Podolski Honey Farms, says the vast majority of honey produced at the family-run business in Ethelbert, Man., is shipped to customers across the United States.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Why are there suddenly so many data centres planned in Canada? Your questions answered
candidates.description: The sudden spike in AI data centres that are planned or under construction in Canada is sparking controversy among those hesitant to have the massive buildings that power this technology humming away in their backyards. We answered some of your questions here.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Ontario businesses brace for tariffs after U.S.-Canada trade talks collapse
candidates.description: Some businesses in Ontario are bracing for tarrifs but pledging steadfastness after Canadian and U.S. trade negotiators came close, but ultimately failed at the 11th hour to reach a trade agreement Friday night.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Ontario judge snubs province's new bail rules by releasing woman without cash deposit
candidates.description: An Ontario Superior Court judge has released a woman charged with human trafficking on bail but without requiring a cash deposit, despite new provincial rules that demand payment in full within 48 hours.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Shelter in place lifted, 2 people arrested after shooting that injured 3 in Fort Smith, N.W.T.
candidates.description: A lockdown order in Fort Smith, N.W.T., has lifted after more than 13 hours, and police say it's now safe for residents to resume normal activities.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Read Mark Carney's full speech after trade talks with the U.S. collapsed
candidates.description: Below are Prime Minister Mark Carney's remarks after Canada suspended trade talks with the U.S. and the Trump administration imposed new 50 per cent tariffs:
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Montrealers march to denounce violence against women after 2 killed in 1 week
candidates.description: Dozens of Montrealers marched in solidarity over violence against women. It comes after two Montreal women were killed last week in separate incidents of suspected intimate partner violence. The march, organized by Maison d'Haïti, took place in the borough of the recent killings, in Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Why a B.C. wildfire evacuee wants to see an overhaul of emergency support services
candidates.description: Dawne Young, a retired 911 dispatcher, said her evacuation experience was unsettling. Her neighbour's home was lost in the Bald Range wildfire. She said her family did not all receive the emergency alert, and she was met with lengthy delays trying to register as an evacuee.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: National 2SLGBTQ+ monument holds special meaning for those purged from civil service for being gay
candidates.description: Thousands of Canadians were purged from the military, RCMP and civil service between the Cold War-era and the 1990s for their sexuality, including Vancouver's Wayne Davis and the great uncle of Elenore Sturko, an MLA and former Mountie.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Churchill, Man., residents say year-round shipping would benefit town but tourism, environment must be considered
candidates.description: Churchill, Man., residents are welcoming findings suggesting a longer shipping season is possible but say any expansion must weigh the impacts on tourism and the environment.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Lunenburg to La-La Land: Logan Taylor chases lifelong NFL dream
candidates.description: Lunenburg, N.S., native Logan Taylor moved away from home at 14 to pursue his NFL dream because his high school didn't have a football program. His journey has included stops in Timberlea, N.S., Virginia and Massachusetts. Now he's in Los Angeles after being drafted by the Chargers.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: A grim property search, 3 grieving families and 'a lot of questions' in this eastern Ontario area
candidates.description: The remains of a third man have been found on a rural property north of the normally quiet eastern Ontario town of Smiths Falls, yet police — who say "they are doing everything they can to bring answers" — aren't linking their deaths. Here's a timeline and what to know about the case as the men's families and the community await answers.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Family grieving Montreal man’s death demands justice after police intervention
candidates.description: The family of Abisay Cruz is demanding to know why Montreal police used a controversial restraint method during the intervention that contributed to his death, saying a newly released coroner's report failed to explain why officers applied a method the police service says it does not teach.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Survivor describes moments after plane ripped through his vehicle in Prince George, B.C.
candidates.description: One person is dead and the Transportation Safety Board is investigating after a plane made an emergency landing on a Prince George, B.C., road on Thursday.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Stabbing at Edmonton Sikh temple leaves 2 injured, man in custody
candidates.description: The World Sikh Organization of Canada said a “violent incident” at the Nanaksar Gurdwara temple in northeast Edmonton Friday morning left two people injured.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Trump says Canada 'wants the benefits' of being a U.S. state 'without being one' as trade dispute deepens
candidates.description: In his first comments since trade talks broke down, President Donald Trump said Canada "wants the benefits" of being a U.S. state "without being one." The president's brief post on his Truth Social platform early Sunday comes after new 50 per cent U.S. tariffs on a range of Canadian goods took effect.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Israeli settler blockades part of escalating violence against Palestinians in the occupied West Bank
candidates.description: A Palestinian-American has returned to his home in the occupied West Bank village of Qusra to protect it from Israeli settlers, amid a surge in attacks and settlement expansion.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Zelenskyy says holding elections during war would 'destroy' Ukraine
candidates.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy says holding elections as active fighting with Russia continues would "split Ukraine." His warning comes after ousted former Ukrainian Defence Minister Mykhailo Fedorov last week called for a wartime vote.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: How will the British press cover Harry and Meghan this time around?
candidates.description: Many questions have already been asked about the couple's return — but after being away for years following a tumultuous relationship with the British press that appeared to have been a factor in their decamping to California, could the tabloids' fascination about the couple peter out this time?
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Zelenskyy vows response to deadly Russian multi-drone attack on shopping centre in central Ukraine
candidates.description: At least 16 people were killed and more than 130 wounded on Friday when several Russian drones struck a ‌shopping centre in central Ukraine, authorities said, with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy promising a response to what he called an "act of barbarism."
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Accused in Tupac Shakur murder trial says nephew fired the fatal shots in 1996 drive-by shooting
candidates.description: Jurors on Thursday heard Duane (Keffe D) Davis tell detectives in an audio recording of a 2008 police interview that his nephew Orlando (Baby Lane) Anderson fired the shots that killed rapper Tupac Shakur. Davis is accused of orchestrating the 1996 killing of the 25-year-old hip-hop superstar.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Canada's an agricultural superpower. Could it feed the whole world?
candidates.description: Experts say that red tape, infrastructure bottlenecks and labour shortages are among the factors undermining Canada's ability to send more food around the world, while competing countries continue to scale up their exports.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Trump says Canada wants 'benefits' of being US state after trade talks collapse
candidates.description: Canada's PM said he was "reluctantly" announcing retaliatory tariffs and accused the US of starting a trade war.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: France links rise in drownings to heatwaves
candidates.description: A government minister says people have been taking risks by going into the water, with 301 deaths since 19 June.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Thousands struggling without power in Indiana 12 days after severe storms
candidates.description: In the town of Gary, where a third of residents live in poverty, people say they have been living in "survival mode".
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Kejelcha breaks men's half marathon world record by 29 seconds
candidates.description: Ethiopia's Yomif Kejelcha breaks the men's half marathon world record in a time of 56 minutes 51 seconds in a World Athletics road race in Buenos Aires.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Golf brand apologises for advert that shows woman being pushed over
candidates.description: Content creator Good Good apologises and removes an advert that shows a woman being pushed to the ground as she reached for a man's golf club.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Father leaves 7-year-old son alone on Mount Fuji to continue hike
candidates.description: The man had taken his two boys on the trip but is said to have left one behind when he got tired.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Syria says Israeli strike near Damascus violation of international law
candidates.description: The latest incident comes days after reports emerged Israel had struck a military airbase close to the Turkish border.

candidates.title: Rescuers dig through Ukraine mall wreckage as Zelensky condemns 'despicable' Russian strike
candidates.description: Four people are still missing after Friday's attack which killed 16 and left 130 injured, including a number of children.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: US military newspaper editor voices censorship fears after being fired
candidates.description: Erik Slavin believes he was fired for saying in an interview that "in a hypothetical situation, censorship would be a red line".
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: TikTok to pay $400m to US in one of largest child privacy settlements
candidates.description: The deal stems from a 2024 lawsuit alleging TikTok and its parent company ByteDance collected "vast amounts of data" on millions of users under the age of 13.

candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Wicker Man director's sons complete their late father's film trilogy
candidates.description: The final film in the folk horror trilogy brings closure to the saga as well as its creator's family after more than 50 years.

candidates.title: Drugs at their fingertips, intense pressure: Why child stars fall into addiction

candidates.title: How Israel is expanding settlements in drive to reshape West Bank

candidates.title: 'Quiet, quiet, quiet!' - What triggers Trump to shut down reporters?
candidates.description: As the US president insults a journalist again, the BBC looks at the questions he does not like to answer.

candidates.description: Australia has passed a law requiring major tech platforms such as Google and Meta to strike deals with Australian news publishers or pay a levy on their advertising revenue.

candidates.title: Chinese company flexes dominance in robotics space with splashy stock market debut
candidates.description: The Chinese robotics company Unitree, known for its highly advanced humanoid robots, made a tremendous debut on Shanghai's stock market. The company is considered an industry leader in robotics.

candidates.title: The U.S. & Canada are fighting over tariffs. How is that affecting small businesses?
candidates.description: NPR's Danielle Kurtzleben speaks with Mike Roach and Kim Osgood, owners of Paloma Clothing in Portland, Ore., about how the tariff fight between the U.S. and Canada is affecting their business.

candidates.title: Nonprofits are helping musicians pay for insurance in Austin, Texas, and beyond
candidates.description: A nonprofit and a local public health agency are subsidizing marketplace health insurance for Austin musicians , even as rising healthcare costs make the program more expensive.

candidates.title: Becerra, running for governor of California, faces a health insurance problem
candidates.description: The nation's uninsured rate hit a historical low when Xavier Becerra was health secretary. Now he wants to be California's next governor as Trump's actions have driven people off health insurance.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: How to think about this summer's slate of food safety recalls
candidates.description: NPR's David Folkenflik talks with Don Schaffner, a food microbiology specialist and distinguished professor at Rutgers University, about this summer's foodborne illnesses and recalls.
candidates.author: NPR
